document.title: Open Cognitive Bubbles for Communal Problem Solving
document.purpose: Describe a system in which people selectively open parts of their AI-extended thinking environments to shared problems while retaining control over identity, memory, disclosure, endorsement, and participation.

core_insight.observation: A personal AI can expand an individual's effective memory, accessible knowledge, working context, mechanical reasoning, synthesis, and capacity to explore unfamiliar domains.
core_insight.conceptual_move: Instead of placing several people inside one centralized AI workspace, allow each person to open a governed aperture from their private AI-extended thinking space into a shared problem space.
short_formulations: Open your AI-extended thinking bubble to a shared problem.
Communal problem solving through interoperating cognitive extensions.
A governed aperture between private augmented cognition and shared knowledge.
Shared problem memory without centralized ownership of every mind, model, or contribution.

cognitive_bubble.definition: A personally controlled environment consisting of a person, their private memory and materials, and AI capabilities applied to that context.

shared_problem_space.definition: A persistent, collectively accessible environment organized around a problem rather than a single project, application, organization, or central assistant.

aperture.definition: A governed and inspectable boundary through which a person and their AI can expose selected capabilities or contributions to a shared problem without exposing the entire private cognitive bubble.
controls: what may leave the private environment
whether AI may only prepare or may also publish
how contributions may be corrected, retracted, or withdrawn

contribution.definition: A bounded, attributable object deliberately exposed to the shared problem space.

problem_memory.definition: The evolving network of contributions, provenance, relationships, evaluations, disagreements, and historical changes associated with a shared problem.
problem_memory.important_constraint: Problem memory should not imply a single universally canonical truth. It should preserve who asserted what, under which evidence, authority, time, visibility, and confidence.

boundary_functions.outward: Transform relevant private work into a bounded, inspectable contribution with provenance, uncertainty, and endorsement status.
boundary_functions.inward: Translate new communal developments into context relevant to the person's own knowledge, goals, hypotheses, and work.
boundary_functions.lateral: Identify potentially valuable connections between independently controlled cognitive bubbles without automatically disclosing their private contents.

participation_levels.name: availability
participation_levels.description: The participant signals that they or their AI may have relevant knowledge or capacity.

participation_levels.name: mediated_query
participation_levels.description: Authorized questions may be submitted, but the personal AI and disclosure policy determine whether and how they can be answered.

participation_levels.name: reviewed_contribution
participation_levels.description: The AI may prepare a contribution, but the person explicitly reviews and publishes it.

participation_levels.name: bounded_delegation
participation_levels.description: The AI may monitor and contribute within explicit scopes, provenance requirements, rate limits, and revocable permissions.

authorship_and_endorsement.principle: AI preparation, human authorship, publication authority, and endorsement must remain distinguishable.

not: automatic pooling of everyone's private memory
a single authority silently determining truth
a requirement that everyone use the same model or application
instead: interoperating but independently controlled cognitive bubbles
shared memory composed from signed contributions and explicit relationships

atproto_hypothesis.role: ATProto may provide an interoperability and sovereignty layer between cognitive bubbles and shared problem spaces, rather than serving as the complete reasoning or private-memory system.
potential_uses: shared Lexicon schemas for contribution types
independently sourced labels, evaluations, or annotations

possible_network_shape.source_layer: Personal and institutional repositories containing signed contribution records.
possible_network_shape.aggregation_layer: Relays, indexes, and problem-specific aggregators discover and connect compatible records.
possible_network_shape.interpretation_layer: Independent problem AppViews produce current frontiers, contradiction maps, evidence networks, and working contexts.
possible_network_shape.interaction_layer: Specialized clients support research, programming, experiments, comparison, critique, decision making, and public explanation.

limitations: Private working memory may require infrastructure beyond public repositories.
Group ownership and governance of problem identities remain unresolved.
The protocol does not decide what constitutes consensus or accepted knowledge.
Scientific and regulatory audit requirements may need stronger retention semantics.
Reproducible AI compute requires preservation of models, tools, parameters, environments, and source inputs beyond basic contribution text.
A dominant aggregator or AppView could recreate centralization at the interpretation layer.

problem_identity_models.description: A problem is identified by a stable record created by an individual or institution.
problem_identity_models.risk: The creator may appear to own the problem.

problem_identity_models.description: A problem space has a persistent identity controlled through community governance.
problem_identity_models.risk: Governance, membership, key control, and dispute resolution are difficult.

problem_identity_models.description: Problems emerge from clusters of semantically related contributions without a single owner.
problem_identity_models.risk: Different formulations may be incorrectly merged or unnecessarily fragmented.

problem_identity_models.description: Governed communities maintain stable problem identifiers while independent AppViews may cluster, split, or relate problems differently.
problem_identity_models.risk: Competing taxonomies improve plurality but increase navigation and interoperability complexity.

primary_risks: confusion between AI generation and human endorsement
dominance by actors able to deploy more compute
insecure or malicious tools inside personal AI environments
historical contributions remaining after a participant wishes to withdraw
design_principles: plural evaluation rather than one hidden ranking authority
human approval for consequential publication or semantic mutation
separate withdrawal from retraction, deletion, and historical preservation

changes: The persistent object shifts from a project toward a problem or question.
The central primitive shifts from project checkout toward a governed aperture between private and shared cognition.
Participants need not belong permanently to one project or organization.
Each participant may use a different AI, memory system, hosting provider, and application.
The shared space preserves plural claims and authorities rather than one canonical organizational state.
Decentralization becomes functionally relevant because participation is open, shifting, and cross-institutional.

smallest_testable_prototype.name: Open Problem Aperture
smallest_testable_prototype.goal: Test whether personal AI environments can exchange useful, bounded contributions to a shared problem without requiring participants to expose their full private context or use one centralized assistant.
smallest_testable_prototype.participants: A small group working on one bounded technical or research problem.
minimum_flow: Each participant has a private source collection and AI workspace.
A shared problem record defines the current question and contribution schema.
Participants authorize their AI to prepare, but not automatically publish, candidate contributions.
Each outbound contribution displays source provenance, uncertainty, AI involvement, and endorsement status.
The shared layer connects related and contradictory contributions.
Each personal AI receives only relevant shared updates and explains why they matter to its participant.
Participants may revoke future access without silently rewriting the meaning of past public claims.
smallest_testable_prototype.comparison: Compare against a shared chat containing the same participants and source material.
smallest_testable_prototype.core_hypothesis: Interoperating personal AI environments will produce broader, better-grounded, and more reusable collective reasoning than a centralized shared chat, while preserving clearer authority and privacy boundaries.
success_signals: participants contribute useful knowledge that would otherwise remain private or unexpressed
shared updates are relevant rather than overwhelming
participants understand what their AI disclosed
human and AI authorship remain distinguishable
later work can reuse contributions without reconstructing the entire conversation
falsification_signals: the disclosure workflow costs more effort than ordinary collaboration
participants do not trust the aperture
the shared chat performs equally well
meaningful knowledge cannot be separated from private context
participants cannot understand or control what their AI reveals
provenance and endorsement requirements make contributions too cumbersome
aggregation centralizes authority despite decentralized storage

hard_questions_for_sparring: Is the cognitive bubble a real architectural object or only a metaphor for a personal AI workspace?
What exact capabilities can be exposed without exposing source content?
Can an AI answer mediated queries without leaking facts through inference, wording, confidence, or refusal behavior?
Who defines or governs a shared problem identity?
What is the minimum interoperable contribution schema?
Does each contribution need to be public, or can the network support restricted and encrypted problem spaces?
How is human endorsement represented when an AI performed most of the reasoning?
Can participants meaningfully revoke AI access after derived knowledge has entered communal memory?
How does the system resist thousands of low-quality automated contributions?
How are minority, dissenting, and superseded positions preserved without overwhelming users?
Can independent AppViews disagree productively about relevance, quality, and problem structure?
What prevents the dominant AppView from becoming the de facto central authority?
Would researchers and programmers accept contribution objects, or prefer existing papers, repositories, issues, and chats?
What immediate personal benefit motivates someone to open their bubble?
Which bounded problem would provide a decisive prototype test?

classification: requires a narrow use case and falsifiable prototype
current_verdict.strongest_claim: The central opportunity is not merely collective project memory. It is a governed interface through which independently controlled, AI-extended human cognition can participate in persistent communal problem solving.
current_verdict.main_uncertainty: Whether useful shared knowledge can cross the aperture with sufficiently low effort, high trust, strong provenance, and meaningful privacy.
current_verdict.recommended_next_focus: Specify and prototype the aperture contract before building a complete problem-memory protocol, dynamic interface system, or decentralized platform.
